statutory_penalty_tiers.title: Breach of Essential Cybersecurity Requirements & Core Manufacturer Obligations
statutory_penalty_tiers.scope: Non-compliance with essential cybersecurity requirements laid down in Annex I (security-by-design, default configurations, vulnerability handling) and manufacturer obligations laid down in Article 13(1)-(20).
statutory_penalty_tiers.applicability: Manufacturers, importers, and distributors of products with digital elements.
aggravating_factors: Duration and gravity of the infringement
Intentional or negligent character of the breach
Failure to report actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours
Number of affected users or devices in the internal market
mitigating_factors: Timely and proactive notification to CSIRT / ENISA
Immediate roll-out of security patches at no cost to users

statutory_penalty_tiers.title: Breach of General Obligations & Reporting Procedures
statutory_penalty_tiers.scope: Non-compliance with obligations laid down in Articles 14 (incident reporting), 15, 18, 19, 21, and 23 (importer, distributor, and representative obligations).
aggravating_factors: Failure to maintain technical documentation or SBOM for 10 years
mitigating_factors: Early identification and remediation of procedural gaps

statutory_penalty_tiers.title: Misleading, Incomplete, or False Information to Regulators
statutory_penalty_tiers.scope: Supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information to market surveillance authorities or notified bodies in response to an official request.
statutory_penalty_tiers.applicability: Any economic operator subject to CRA requests.
aggravating_factors: Concealment of known critical vulnerabilities or exploited backdoors

sme_microenterprise_provisions.summary: When determining administrative fines for SMEs and microenterprises, market surveillance authorities must take into account their size and economic viability, ensuring fines remain proportionate and non-confiscatory.

incident_vulnerability_reporting_timelin.recipient: CSIRTs network & ENISA Single Reporting Platform

stages.trigger: Becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident affecting the product with digital elements.
stages.required_content: Indication whether the event is suspected of being caused by malicious acts and whether it has international impact.
General description of the vulnerability/incident, initial severity assessment, impacted components, and available mitigations.

stages.trigger: Upon request of CSIRT or ENISA.
stages.required_content: Detailed technical analysis of exploitation status, affected user base, and corrective measures underway.
Root cause analysis, detailed remediation summary, permanent patch PURLs, and lessons learned.

product_conformity_tiers.assessment_procedure: Internal control (Module A) — self-assessment by manufacturer.

product_conformity_tiers.category: Important Products with Digital Elements — Class I (Annex III)
product_conformity_tiers.assessment_procedure: Application of harmonised standards (Module A) OR third-party EU-type examination (Module B + C).

product_conformity_tiers.category: Important Products with Digital Elements — Class II (Annex IV)
product_conformity_tiers.assessment_procedure: Mandatory third-party conformity assessment (Module B + C) or full quality assurance (Module H).

product_conformity_tiers.category: Critical Products with Digital Elements (Annex V)
examples: Operating systems for critical infrastructure entities
product_conformity_tiers.assessment_procedure: Mandatory European cybersecurity certification scheme (EUCC) at level 'high'.

mandatory_sbom_requirements.obligation: Manufacturers must draw up a software bill of materials (SBOM) identifying and documenting all top-level and transitive software components and dependencies.
